items.title: Hearings not taking place for years: Supreme Court flags serious concerns with consumer forums, seeks report
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday frowned upon the performance of consumer commissions across the country for the inordinate amount of time taken by them to decide consumer cases/ complaints. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also took note of a newspaper report which termed the performance of consumer forums as "pitiful and poor". In many pending matters, hearings do not take place for years, the Court noted. "The moment you start paying for case disposal, you will see how the disposal will multiply. The moment you keep on adding more and more infrastructure, the courts and facilities, then unfortunately this is the outcome. There is a newspaper report also in which the following issues have been highlighted with respect to the pitiful and poor performance of the Consumer Commissions, including the National Consumer Commission. The inordinate delay in disposal of the pending matters, especially when even hearings are not taking place for years," the Court said. items.title: Bowing to corporate pressure? Supreme Court slams FSSAI's reluctance to put warning labels on foods high in sugar, salt, fat
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned the reluctance of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce front-of-pack warning labels on packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan was hearing a case in which the Court had earlier urged the FSSAI to consider introducing such warning labels in the interest of public health. Today, the Court took critical note that the FSSAI was hesitant to implement such a measure, going by a the minutes of a meeting held by the food standards watchdog. The Court asked if the FSSAI was bowing down to corporate entities involved in food manufacture. " Are you taking the court for a toss? ... There is immense pressure at the end of all these corporate houses on you. And you are succumbing to that pressure! We are doing this in public interest. Keep it in mind. We are not doing it for ourselves. Why are you not abiding by our order? What have you done so far? We know the pressure on you.
